_comment: Pinned playbook identity anchors. One write-once doc per `playbook_id` (`spb-<16hex>`) normally, `_id == playbook_id`. `anchor_centroid` is the size-weighted, L2-normalised group centroid captured the first time the id was minted during the `name playbooks` pass — it is NEVER updated, so `_assign_playbook_id` matches against a fixed reference rather than a walking latest-centroid. This prevents transitive id chaining (A~B>=thr, B~C>=thr, A~C<thr collapsing under one id). `predicate_signature` (item 30) is a modal/frequency vector of the 7 structural predicates (src/enrich/sources/cowrie/predicates.py) over the anchor's member sessions, unindexed like `anchor_centroid` — read only by the below-tau rescue tier in assignment.py, never queried. `seed_playbook_id` records the membership hash that minted this anchor (audit trail). `is_satellite` (item 59, gated off by `anchor_satellite_minting_enabled`) marks a doc minted for an ALREADY-named `playbook_id` whose original anchor has drifted below `assignment_tau` of its own newer members — its `_id` is `<playbook_id>-sat-<8hex>` (distinct from `playbook_id`) so the index is no longer strictly one doc per id, but `_assign_playbook_id`/`assignment.py` already argmax over every loaded anchor and return the winning anchor's `playbook_id`, so satellites resolve identically to the primary on the read side. Created by `init-indexes --source cowrie`; populated as playbooks are named. Independent of the session_clusters index, so cluster-doc replacement across backward cycles can't move anchors. E4 (Finding 76) adds a narrow, gated exception to write-once: when `mint_predicate_split` is enabled and a group's members split cleanly on the structural predicates, the parent anchor is RE-PINNED onto the members it retained while the minority is force-minted as its own id. Without the re-pin both halves sit at cosine ~0.99 of the original centroid and the split is a no-op. This is not the walking centroid write-once guards against — the id is unchanged and the centroid moves AWAY from members it lost, never toward a neighbouring anchor. `repinned_from_centroid` keeps the prior vector so the write is reversible, `repin_count` makes repeated re-pinning of one anchor visible, and `repinned_at` / `repinned_run_id` / `repin_reason` attribute it. An anchor with no `repin_*` fields has never been re-pinned.
